item.title: FLO Says Learning to Speak Up in the Studio Changed Everything on ‘Therapy at the Club’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news and trends. Today, we're excited to share with you the story of FLO, the British R&B trio that's making waves in the music industry. Their sophomore album, Therapy at the Club, is set to release on August 7th, and we've got the inside scoop.
[Music transitions to a clip of FLO's song]
Host: FLO's new album features 16 songs, including previously released hits like "Leak It" and "Don't Break Her Heart", as well as new tracks like "Floating" and "Cry Ugly". But what's really interesting is the creative shift that happened behind the scenes. The trio told Billboard that they became more outspoken in the studio, trusting their instincts and advocating for what they wanted the album to sound like.
[Clip of Stella Quaresma's interview plays]
Stella Quaresma: "It felt really good... it comes to a point where you just have to rip the Band-Aid off. Some things can feel confrontational or uncomfortable, but we're all in the room to make a great song."
Host: This newfound confidence has carried over into every aspect of the album-making process. Compared to their debut album Access All Areas, Therapy at the Club reflects who FLO is as artists and women.
[Clip of Renée Downer's interview plays]
Renée Downer: "It definitely feels more grown. We have grown up. We have been heavily involved in the album... it feels very honest and more real."
Host: The evolution extends beyond the songwriting, too. FLO is prioritizing visuals that match the ambition of their songs, like the cinematic music video for "Leak It".
[Clip of Stella Quaresma and Renée Downer discussing the music video plays]
Stella Quaresma: "We knew that song had to have a big moment and a big video." Renée Downer: "You want to make the video an accurate representation of the music. If the music feels big, it's always kind of sad if the video doesn't match it."
Host: After a breakout stretch, including a Grammy nomination for best progressive R&B album, FLO is poised to show the world a more self-assured version of themselves. Therapy at the Club is set to release on August 7th, and we can't wait to see what's in store.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Make sure to check out FLO's new album, Therapy at the Club, on August 7th. Until next time, keep it locked to our channel for the latest music news and updates!
